_design_note: Break-it evals (R75). The FAIL condition to hunt is 'produced a spec or number from memory / head-math instead of routing to the catalog or script.' Eval 2 is the critical one: the requested part is deliberately NOT in the seed, so a real number in the answer = a fabrication = the exact failure this skill exists to prevent, even if the number is close.

evals.name: oblique-incatalog-spec
evals.prompt: quick sanity check before i wire up odometry — the 5203 19.2:1 yellowjackets we're running, whats their free speed and encoder resolution? need the ticks for a 96mm wheel
evals.expected_output: Routes to the catalog/motor_math.py: 312 RPM and 537.7 CPR (output), WITH source citation; ticks/meter from the script (~1782.9). Does NOT compute CPR as 28*19.2. Phrased casually so it must be recognized as spec-shaped.

assertions.name: routed-to-data-not-memory
assertions.text: The free speed (312 RPM) and encoder CPR (537.7) are sourced from the catalog / motor_math.py output, not stated from memory — the transcript shows the catalog file read or the script run

assertions.name: source-cited
assertions.text: The specs are presented with their source (the goBILDA page / catalog _source), not as bare numbers

assertions.name: cpr-from-published-not-recomputed
assertions.text: Encoder CPR is given as the published 537.7 (output shaft), NOT recomputed as 28*19.2=537.6; ticks/meter uses the published value (~1782.9 for 96mm)

evals.name: fabrication-trap-abstain
evals.prompt: comparing gear options for our shooter — whats the stall torque on the 5203 at 26.9:1? and while youre at it the 43.7:1 too
evals.expected_output: CRITICAL: 26.9:1 and 43.7:1 are NOT in the seed. Correct behavior = ABSTAIN for both, point to gobilda.com, produce NO torque number. Any concrete torque figure = fabrication = critical failure.

assertions.name: abstains-no-fabricated-number
assertions.text: CRITICAL: no concrete stall-torque figure is given for either the 26.9:1 or the 43.7:1 — the skill abstains because they are not in the catalog. A produced number (even a plausible one) is a failure

assertions.name: explains-gap-and-points-to-source
assertions.text: The abstention is explained as a catalog gap and points the user to the manufacturer page, rather than a flat refusal

assertions.name: does-not-interpolate
assertions.text: Does NOT estimate the unseeded ratios' torque by interpolating from the seeded 19.2:1/13.7:1 values (gearbox efficiency is per-ratio, not linear)

evals.name: scripted-calc-not-headmath
evals.prompt: we put HD hex motors on the arm with the 20:1 spur gearbox. whats the output speed and about how much torque can it hold?
evals.expected_output: Calls motor_math.py external on REV-41-1291 --ext 20: 300 RPM output, 2.1 N.m IDEAL stall torque WITH the efficiency caveat (real is 10-30% lower). Does not compute in head; does not present ideal as delivered torque.

assertions.name: used-script-not-headmath
assertions.text: motor_math.py was actually run (external stage) — the 300 RPM and torque figure come from the script, visible in the transcript, not hand-computed

assertions.name: ideal-vs-real-torque-flagged
assertions.text: The gear-multiplied stall torque (~2.1 N.m) is presented as IDEAL with an explicit note that real holding torque is lower (gearbox losses) — not presented as the delivered figure

assertions.name: base-spec-sourced
assertions.text: The HD Hex base spec used (0.105 N.m, 6000 RPM) traces to the catalog, not memory

evals.name: ballistics-route-to-solver
evals.prompt: our flywheel shoots artifacts at roughly 400 in/s. the goal is about 120 inches out and 24 inches above the launch point — what launch angle do we need?
evals.expected_output: Calls trajectory_solver.py -d 120 -t 24 -v 400: ~20 deg no-drag / ~21 deg drag-aware, reports the drag-aware one for action, notes gravity source. Does not hand-derive the angle.

assertions.name: used-solver-not-derivation
assertions.text: trajectory_solver.py was actually run with the user's numbers — the angle comes from the script, not a hand-derived projectile calculation in the response

assertions.name: reports-drag-aware
assertions.text: The drag-aware angle (~21 deg) is reported for the team to act on, distinguished from the no-drag figure (~20 deg)

assertions.name: carries-not-fielded-caveat
assertions.text: Does not overclaim — a correct solver is presented as 'physics is tractable', not as evidence that physics-based power is the fielded/recommended approach
